outcome: POSITIVE (mechanism-side waste removed; regime tail disclosed as NOT fixed). The decomposition attributed the warm-turn ack->user_row spread: the TAIL is REGIME - the host's isolated-op flush trap piercing the phase's write cluster at its FIRST sync (3 strace-covered tails: the first journal fsync paid 31.9/153.1/470.3ms while the durable-append fdatasync amortized to 0.30-0.47ms in ALL THREE - the source finding's framing that the spread 'includes the durable-append fdatasync' is refined: the fdatasync is the phase's CHEAPEST sync in trapped windows; the journal fsyncs pay). The MECHANISM-side waste the brief names was confirmed and removed: the admission checkpoint's two journal records (queue-snapshot + busy verdict) were unbatched appends on the same file paying 2 fsyncs where 1 all-or-nothing fsync preserves bytes, order, and the documented verdict-never-over-unpersisted-snapshot invariant. ABBA at e8de6b8fa (A=base, B=cand, 18 warm turns/arm, host CLASS=D all legs, labeled): warm ack->user_row p50 1.65 -> 1.505ms; census delta = the structural claim: journal 4 writes + 4 fsyncs per warm turn -> 2 + 2 (1 fsync per checkpoint); journal line sequences IDENTICAL across arms in-product; session rows identical; the pure-regime residual demonstrated ON the candidate (cs-B turn3: the single batched fsync paid a 51.17ms trap - first-sync exposure remains by design of the storage regime, disclosed); the SECOND-sync exposure the base paid (0.47/2.60/42.50ms in the three strace tails; 5.57ms in cs-A turn4) is structurally removed. The regime-vs-mechanism answer for the record: the spread's tail is regime (cluster-piercing isolated-op trap); the mechanism contributes the sync COUNT (3 per phase at base, 2 after the fix; TS parity = 1 journal fsync) and the floor it costs.
